findings.message:
[P2] Canonicalize the fixture install path before invoking the installer

`root` is created under the test's `TMPDIR` and the fixture installs the legacy helper at `$root/bin/gpg-dsh 'fixture`. On macOS `tmpdir()` is `/var/folders/...` and `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`, so `scripts/install-gpg-dsh.sh` resolves the parent with `pwd -P` and rejects the path through its canonical-path equality check, exiting 2 before it drains; `start_installer` then fails with `installer exited without draining`. Since `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` maps to `needsDarwinTests`, this breaks the darwin job even though the same test passes on Linux. Canonicalizing the fixture root (for example `root=$(cd $root && pwd -P)`) keeps the installer's refusal of symlinked parents while making the fixture portable.

tests/fixtures/gpg-dsh-migration.sh:11-11

[P2] Widen ps args before matching the queued gate marker

`ps -p $new_pid -o args=` is not widened with `-ww`, so where `ps` clips the argument list to the display width (macOS uses the terminal width and falls back to 80 columns when stdout is not a terminal) the long inline `-c` program passed by the gate means the `gpg-dsh-install-wait` marker at the end of argv is cut off. The loop then times out with `new signing did not reach the installation barrier` even though the gate is correctly queued; the installer already uses `ps -axww` for the same reason. Use `ps -ww -p ...` so the barrier observation survives argument clipping.

tests/fixtures/gpg-dsh-migration.sh:144-144

summary: The change adds an owner-run installer that fences the installed gpg-dsh entrypoint with a temporary queue, drains live legacy helper and gpg processes plus a live legacy rebuild lock, then atomically publishes the repository helper, together with migration documentation and a fixture wired into tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts. The installer logic and the Linux fixture flow look sound, but the new fixture cannot pass on the darwin job: its installed path is derived from the symlinked macOS temp root, which the installer's canonical-path check rejects, and its gate observation uses an un-widened ps invocation that can drop the gpg-dsh-install-wait marker.

evidence: scripts/install-gpg-dsh.sh fences the installed entrypoint with <path>.install-lock, drains this user's legacy helper and gpg processes plus a live legacy lock owner, then publishes the repository helper and restores the original on timeout.

tests/fixtures/gpg-dsh-migration.sh pauses the legacy rebuild at a copy barrier, starts the installer and a queued signing call, resumes the legacy call and requires install=0 new=0 legacy=0 lock-and-stage-preserved=true.
tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:813-820 wires the fixture into the focused helper suite, and docs/gpg-dsh-migration.md documents the owner-run quiescence procedure and failure recovery.
Abandoned legacy copy removal, ownership checks, seeded-config refusal and the existing per-user layout remain unchanged in ops/gpg-dsh.sh and are asserted by the fixture at lines 195-219.
